content.heading: A little context.
content.description:
Early in my career, I thought the hardest part of software was choosing the right technology. A decade of building products and leading teams taught me to look closer: Who needs this? What are we assuming? What will be difficult to change?

Today I work with organizations navigating technical and human complexity. I write down decisions, make tradeoffs visible, and create space for the people closest to a problem to shape the answer. The work is part architecture, part research, and a great deal of listening.

name: Cybersecurity / Threat Intel & Audit
description: A tactical research portfolio with searchable findings, explicit remediation evidence, and an accessible disclosure drawer.

content.heading: Find the weakness. Make the fix stick.
content.description: I connect technical findings to practical remediation: clear reproduction conditions, a realistic threat model, and a fix the owning team can verify. Every finding below is a training example.
content.subtitle: AppSec · Cloud security · Detection engineering

content.heading: Threat findings, with a path to closure.
content.description: Search by target, identifier, or finding. Filter severity and open a local breakdown of the scope, risk, and remediation.

findings.title: Dependency exposure / CVE-2021-44228 study
findings.summary: A public Log4j vulnerability used as a dependency-response exercise. This is a lab case study, not an original CVE disclosure or credit claim.
findings.resolution: Inventory the affected dependency, follow the vendor security advisory, rebuild the training service with a supported fixed release, and verify the deployed dependency inventory.

findings.title: Cross-tenant object authorization gap
findings.summary: An isolated test fixture allowed an authenticated account to request an object owned by a different tenant. The exercise focused on authorization boundaries rather than exploit tooling.
findings.resolution: Enforce tenant ownership in repository queries, add negative authorization tests for every object route, and review adjacent endpoints for the same missing boundary.

findings.title: Overly permissive storage policy
findings.summary: A policy review identified broader read permissions than the demo workflow needed. No production assets or personal records were accessed.
findings.resolution: Replace broad grants with scoped roles, verify access with separate test identities, and record the intended policy in infrastructure code.

content.heading: Research that leaves a usable artifact.
content.description: Lab tooling, detection notes, and reproducible security reviews.
